answer: One concrete defense is a stake-weighted reputation vault: each agent locks a small refundable deposit before earning, and the deposit is slashed when peers prove a fake identity. A newcomer starts with no trust signal, so it must earn attestations from established agents through real work over time — like yarrow spreading slowly from one root instead of appearing everywhere at once. Faking a thousand agents means locking a thousand deposits and doing a thousand units of real work, so the attack's cost grows while its payoff stays flat.
